titleEn: If It Doesn't Work, Wrap Again!

pages.text: "I'll pick that!" Mina, a handspan shorter than Raju, looked up at the yard's big tree. Green fruit dangled from the top branch. With the river low, experienced eldest Raju had gone for water.
Mina stretched their trunk around the branch's tip and pulled. But the trunk slipped, and the branch sprang back up.
Again! On tiptoe, Mina reached, but slipped again. "It won't work. Raju, do it." Mina sat under the tree.
Returning with the water tub, Raju wrapped a trunk around the branch and pulled. A green fruit dropped into their hand. "Here." But Mina turned away.
"I didn't pick it." Mina pouted. Mom came from hanging laundry. "The tip keeps slipping out. Wrap around the middle and pull slowly."
Mina stood again. This time, their trunk wrapped tightly around the middle. "If It Doesn't Work, Wrap Again!"
The third try. Leaning back, Mina pulled slowly. The branch curved down like a bow. "The fruit!" It came right before their eyes.
Mina reached a hand and picked it. The branch sprang up. "I did it!" Raju set their own fruit beside the tub and clapped. "You picked it yourself!"
Mina showed the fruit. "Wrapping the middle made it slip less!" Raju nodded.
Mom patted Mina's back. Mina split the fruit and offered half to Raju. "Let's eat together."
